title: The coming day
summary: Moroni addresses those who do not believe in Christ and asks whether they will deny God when brought before the Lamb of God on the day of visitation.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni speaks concerning those who do not believe in Christ.
Moroni asks whether unbelievers will deny God when the Lord comes and they stand before the Lamb of God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The words can be presented as off-screen narration over a restrained, nonliteral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the Lord, the Lamb of God, and the day of visitation is not specified here.

narration.text: I speak also concerning those who do not believe in Christ.
when ye shall be brought to stand before the Lamb of God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The coming is described in conditional future terms; do not depict it as an event occurring now.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the earth rolling together or elements melting as a present event.

title: Guilt before holiness
summary: Moroni warns that those conscious of guilt and filthiness would be miserable before a holy God and describes what they will be brought to see.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni asks whether those conscious of guilt could be happy dwelling with the holy Being.
Moroni says they would be more miserable dwelling with a holy and just God than with damned souls in hell.
Moroni says they will be brought to see their nakedness before God, the glory of God, and the holiness of Jesus Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Keep the warning as off-screen narration without visualizing the metaphor of an unquenchable flame.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of God or Jesus Christ is not described in this passage.

narration.text: Do ye suppose that ye could be happy to dwell with that holy Being
more miserable to dwell with a holy and just God
the glory of God, and the holiness of Jesus Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The flame language is presented as a consequence in Moroni's warning, not as a narrated visible event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage hell, divine figures, or a literal flame.

title: Turn unto the Lord
summary: Moroni exhorts unbelievers to turn to the Lord and pray to the Father in Jesus's name to be cleansed and found pure at the last day.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni urges unbelievers to turn to the Lord and cry to the Father in Jesus's name.
Moroni describes being found spotless and cleansed by the blood of the Lamb at the last day.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; the cleansing language need not be depicted literally.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity, appearance, and setting of any person hearing this exhortation are unspecified.

narration.text: O then ye unbelieving, turn ye unto the Lord
cry mightily unto the Father in the name of Jesus

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage is an exhortation, not a report of someone praying.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show an invented prayer scene or literal blood cleansing.

title: God is unchanging
summary: Moroni challenges those who deny revelations and spiritual gifts, saying that denying them shows a failure to understand the gospel and scriptures, and argues that God does not change.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni addresses those who say revelations, prophecies, gifts, healing, and tongues have ceased.
Moroni says a denier does not know the gospel of Christ and does not understand the scriptures.
Moroni says God is the same yesterday, today, and forever, without variableness or changing.
Moroni says an imagined changing god is not the God of miracles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the continuous argument as off-screen narration over an unspecified, nonliteral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience and physical setting are not identified.

narration.text: I speak unto you who deny the revelations of God
God is the same yesterday, today, and forever

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a continuous teaching, not an enacted scene of miracles.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a changing deity or imagined miracle.

title: The God of miracles
summary: Moroni identifies the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as Creator, and recounts the creation of Adam, the Fall, and redemption through Jesus Christ.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob created the heavens, earth, and all things in them.
Moroni says God created Adam, the Fall came by Adam, and redemption came through Jesus Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; references to creation and the Fall need not become depicted events.
unspecified_visual_details: No appearance of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Adam, or Jesus Christ is specified here.

narration.text: the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob
because of Jesus Christ came the redemption of man

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are teachings and a summary of past events, not a present-tense creation scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent portrayals or actions for the named historical figures.

title: Resurrection and judgment
summary: Moroni teaches that Christ's death brings resurrection, that all will be awakened and stand before the Lord's bar, and that judgment follows.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says Christ's death brings resurrection and redemption from endless sleep, and all will be awakened and stand before the Lord's bar.
Moroni says the judgment of the Holy One comes, and describes the continuing states of the filthy, righteous, happy, and unhappy.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration rather than depicting the future resurrection or judgment as happening now.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance of the Holy One and the form of the judgment scene are not described.

narration.text: all men shall be awakened by the power of God
And then cometh the judgment of the Holy One upon them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe future events in teaching language.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a courtroom, a visible trumpet, or depictions of the resurrected.

title: God has not ceased
summary: Moroni asks whether the things he has spoken of have passed and answers no, affirming that God has not ceased to be a God of miracles.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni asks whether the things he has spoken of have passed and answers that they have not.
Moroni says God has not ceased to be a God of miracles and asks who can comprehend God's marvelous works.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the questions as off-screen narration over a quiet setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The setting and any audience are not specified.

narration.text: God has not ceased to be a God of miracles
who can comprehend the marvelous works of God?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses argue a teaching; no specific miracle is enacted.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular marvelous work.

title: Creation and mighty works
summary: Moroni points to creation, miracles wrought by God's word, the mighty miracles of Jesus Christ and the apostles, and God's unchanging nature.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni asks who can deny that heaven and earth came to be by God's word and man was created from dust.
Moroni says Jesus Christ and the apostles wrought many mighty miracles.
Moroni says God does not change and is a God of miracles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; the examples are summarized rather than narrated as specific visible events.
unspecified_visual_details: No particular miracle, apostle, or appearance of Jesus Christ is specified.

narration.text: by his word the heaven and the earth should be
Jesus Christ did not many mighty miracles?

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The account names past works but does not identify individual miracles to depict.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent specific miracles or put named historical people physically in the scene.

title: Unbelief and the promise
summary: Moroni says miracles cease among people when they dwindle in unbelief and depart from the right way, then states the promise to those who believe in Christ and ask the Father.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says miracles cease among people because they dwindle in unbelief, depart from the right way, and do not know God.
Moroni says that whoever believes in Christ without doubting will receive what they ask of the Father in Christ's name, a promise to all the earth.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration over an unspecified setting; do not illustrate the promise as a particular miracle.
unspecified_visual_details: The people referred to and the physical setting are unspecified.

narration.text: they dwindle in unbelief, and depart from the right way
this promise is unto all, even unto the ends of the earth

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage teaches a general promise; no prayer or answer is narrated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent petitioners or a granted request.

title: Christ's commission to disciples
summary: Moroni recalls Jesus Christ speaking to his disciples in the hearing of a multitude, commanding them to preach the gospel and declaring the outcomes of belief and unbelief.

explicit_facts.text: Jesus Christ spoke to his disciples, including those who should tarry, in the hearing of the multitude.
Jesus commanded them to go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.
Jesus said the believer who is baptized shall be saved and the one who does not believe shall be damned.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A past teaching moment with Jesus addressing disciples and a listening multitude is supported.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, clothing, appearance, and composition of the crowd are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ

narration.text: in the hearing of the multitude
he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Jesus's direct speech is quoted as a continuous exact excerpt.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add other sayings, disciples' names, or actions.

title: Signs That Follow Believers
summary: The verses promise signs to believers and confirmation of the speaker's words to those who believe in his name without doubting.

explicit_facts.text: Signs promised to believers include casting out devils, speaking with new tongues, taking up serpents, protection from a deadly drink, and recovery for the sick after hands are laid on them.
The speaker promises to confirm his words to whoever believes in his name without doubting.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The promises can be presented as text without depicting the signs as events presently occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance are not given in these verses.

spoken_dialogue.text: And these signs shall follow them that believe
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

spoken_dialogue.text: And whosoever shall believe in my name, doubting nothing, unto him will I confirm all my words, even unto the ends of the earth.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jesus Christ (at Bountiful)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The listed signs are promises, not events narrated as occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify or depict the speaker based on these verses alone.
Do not depict the promised signs as present events.

title: Heed the Lord's words
summary: Moroni warns those who despise the works of the Lord and urges his audience to hearken, ask the Father, believe, and come to the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni asks who can stand against or deny the works and sayings of the Lord.
Moroni warns despisers that they will wonder and perish.
Moroni urges his audience to ask the Father in Jesus's name, believe, and come to the Lord with all their heart.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration over a neutral setting.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific audience or physical location is given.

narration.text: hearken unto the words of the Lord
come unto the Lord with all your heart

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning and exhortation are teaching, not a depicted destruction.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show anyone perishing or invent an audience.

title: Serve the living God
summary: Moroni counsels his audience to be wise, resist temptation, serve God, and partake in baptism and the sacrament worthily and endure to the end.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni tells his audience to be wise, strip themselves of uncleanness, and serve the true and living God without yielding to temptation.
Moroni warns against unworthy baptism and sacrament and says those who do all things worthily and endure to the end will not be cast out.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Present the counsel as off-screen narration rather than inventing a baptism or sacrament ceremony.
unspecified_visual_details: No individuals or ritual setting are identified.

narration.text: serve the true and living God
see that ye do all things in worthiness

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are instructions, not reports that anyone was baptized or partook of the sacrament.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an unspecified baptism, sacrament, or temptation.

title: Words from the dead
summary: Moroni says he speaks as though from the dead, asks that he and his father not be condemned for imperfection, and urges gratitude for the lesson their imperfections provide.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says he speaks as though from the dead and knows his audience will have his words.
Moroni asks that he, his father, and earlier writers not be condemned for imperfection.
Moroni says their imperfections can teach readers to be wiser.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration; do not depict Moroni or his father as visible speakers.
unspecified_visual_details: The manner or setting of Moroni's writing and the identity of earlier writers are unspecified.

narration.text: I speak unto you as though I spake from the dead
Condemn me not because of mine imperfection

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Moroni's phrase is figurative framing for his words, not an account of a visible appearance from the dead.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a ghost or identify Moroni's father beyond the text.

title: The record's language
summary: The writers state that they wrote the record in characters called reformed Egyptian, handed down and altered according to their manner of speech. They say they would have written in Hebrew if the plates had been sufficiently large, but they had altered Hebrew too.

explicit_facts.text: The writers say they wrote the record according to their knowledge in characters called reformed Egyptian, handed down and altered according to their manner of speech.
The writers say they would have written in Hebrew if the plates had been sufficiently large, and that they had altered Hebrew too.
The writers say that if they could have written in Hebrew, the record would have had no imperfection.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A view of the plates could accompany the passage without depicting a writing act.
unspecified_visual_details: The plates' appearance, the characters' appearance, and the location are not described.

narration.text: we have written this record according to our knowledge,
in the characters which are called among us the reformed Egyptian,
if our plates had been sufficiently large we should have written in Hebrew;
but the Hebrew hath been altered by us also;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage explains the record's language and a conditional alternative; it does not narrate a writing act in progress.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed speaker, depict a writing act in progress, or invent legible characters, plate dimensions, or a location.

title: Means for interpretation
summary: The Lord knows what has been written and that no other people know the writers' language; he has prepared means for its interpretation.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord knows the things the writers have written.
No other people know the writers' language.
The Lord has prepared means for its interpretation.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, the form of the writings, and the means of interpretation are not described.

narration.text: But the Lord knoweth the things which we have written, and also that none other people knoweth our language; and because that none other people knoweth our language, therefore he hath prepared means for the interpretation thereof.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not narrate an interpretation event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the writers or depict the Lord appearing.
Do not specify an interpreter, translation instrument, or interpretation event.

title: Prayers for restoration
summary: Moroni says the record was written to answer for those who dwindled in unbelief, describes the desire for their restoration to knowledge of Christ as aligned with the saints' prayers, and offers a closing prayer.

explicit_facts.text: Moroni says the things were written to rid their garments of the blood of their brethren who dwindled in unbelief.
Moroni says their desire for their brethren's restoration to knowledge of Christ accords with the prayers of the saints who lived in the land.
Moroni prays that Jesus Christ grant the prayers' answer according to faith, that God remember the covenant with the house of Israel, and bless them through faith in Jesus Christ.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen narration and prayer; do not depict an unspecified group of saints or brethren.
unspecified_visual_details: The brethren, saints, and land are not identified further, and no visible prayer posture or setting is specified.

narration.text: their restoration to the knowledge of Christ
may the Lord Jesus Christ grant that their prayers may be answered

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The blood language is figurative accountability, not a narrated injury or bloodshed.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict blood on garments, name the brethren, or stage a gathering of saints.
